text:
Alex Green: Starting thread to lock down a 12-month plan for routing policies + multi-region tenant isolation. Goal: fast wins for customers while keeping future dedicated pools possible.

Meena Kapoor: Sounds good. Customers ask for region affinity, clear isolation tiers, and migration docs. We need concrete launch criteria.

Samir Patel: Please define the "logical isolation" boundary so SRE and security know the operational limits.

Jordan Lee: Proposed shorthand:
- soft isolation = namespace + rate limiting + scheduling tags (no dedicated GPUs)
- hard isolation = dedicated pools, isolated networking, separate KMS scopes

Tess Huang: Agree. We should also specify fallback semantics when affinity fails (latency budget, retry policy, and billing implications).

Alex Green: Draft roadmap: Phase A (0-4 mo): routing primitives (policy API, region preference, simple split rules), region affinity enforcement, canary routing. Phase B (4-10 mo): logical isolation (namespaces, quotas, KV cache partitioning, per-tenant metrics). Phase C (10-16 mo): dedicated pool orchestration + legal/contractual isolation features.

Meena Kapoor: Phase A launch checklist (working draft):
- public policy API (v1) documented
- region preference enforced at p95 >= 98%
- percent-based split routing for canaries
- canary + automatic fallback enabled
- migration guide + security checklist published

Samir Patel: Add to checklist: perf test harness baseline + regression alerts for routing changes. Also run chaos tests for cross-region fallbacks.

Jordan Lee: Example policy YAML (Phase A):
```
routing_policy:
  tenant: rdx-718
  region_preference: [eu-west-1, us-east-1]
  isolation_tier: soft
  split_by: percentage
  split_value: 10
  fallback: auto-route
```

Tess Huang: Security note: must include KMS scoping guidance and an audit log of routing decisions per tenant. Customers keep asking about data plane control.

InfraBot: Reminder: run routing policy canary tests on 2026-06-02T03:00Z.

Alex Green: Operational runbook items (for eng-oncall):
- revoke region affinity for tenant (steps + estimated downtime)
- emergency migration to fallback region
- cost attribution when fallback occurs (billing tags and finance hooks)
- per-tenant latency/cost dashboards in Console

Samir Patel: Open risk: cross-region billing and tax implications for fallback traffic. Need finance + legal input.

Meena Kapoor: I'll own the launch checklist and security/regulatory docs. Samir and Jordan to own runbooks and perf harness. Tess, can you draft the KMS guidance?

Tess Huang: Yup. I'll sketch KMS/HSM boundaries and what we promise for private deployments.

Alex Green: Scope negotiation: we defer dedicated GPU orchestration to Phase C but design Phase A APIs to be compatible. Specifically: include a simple "isolation_tier" enum and extensible policy metadata so Phase C can map to dedicated pools without API changes.

Jordan Lee: For canaries/A-B we need split_by: percentage and split_by: header for targeted experiments. Add to Phase A backlog.

Meena Kapoor: Next tactical steps:
1) PM/Infra sync to finalize Phase A API contract (this week)
2) 2-week eng spike to prototype region affinity enforcement
3) Security design review for KMS + audit (3 weeks)
4) Finance sync for cross-region billing model (me)

Finance Team: Will join the sync. We need examples of fallback volume to run cost modeling.

Alex Green: Okay, owners assigned. I'll create a minimal RFC and share it in #product later today. Thanks all :thumbsup:
